The harbour master kept a ledger of every vessel that entered the estuary, noting the tide, the wind, and the number of crates unloaded before dusk. Most entries were unremarkable. On the fourteenth of October he wrote that a small boat had arrived without papers, carrying three passengers and a crate of glassware packed in straw, and that the youngest passenger had asked whether the lighthouse was still manned. He recorded no answer. The ledger passed to his daughter, who kept it in a drawer for forty years, and then to a local museum, where it was catalogued, photographed, and largely forgotten until a graduate student noticed that the handwriting changed halfway through the volume.

Bridge engineers distinguish between the load a structure carries and the load it can be imagined to carry. The first is a matter of arithmetic: the mass of the deck, the traffic, the accumulated weight of snow in a bad winter. The second is a matter of judgement, and it is where the arguments happen. A cable rated for a hundred tonnes will not fail at a hundred and one, but nobody can say precisely where it will fail, and so the margin is chosen by committee, revised after accidents, and defended in language that sounds more certain than the underlying physics warrants.

She had learned to cook from her grandmother, who never measured anything and grew impatient with questions. How much salt? Enough. How long in the oven? Until it smells right. For years this seemed like withholding, a refusal to share what she knew. Later it became obvious that the older woman genuinely could not answer, because the knowledge had never been stored as numbers. It lived in her hands and in the smell of the kitchen, and translating it into a recipe would have destroyed most of what made it work.

The rewilding project began with a fence and an argument about deer. Removing the deer, said one faction, would let the saplings through and the wood would restore itself within a generation. Leaving them, said the other, would preserve the open glades that half the butterfly species depended on. Both were describing real ecosystems; they simply disagreed about which one had a better claim to be the original. After eleven years the fence came down, the deer returned in smaller numbers, and the wood turned out to become something neither faction had predicted.

Compilers spend most of their effort on code nobody reads. A programmer writes a loop; the compiler unrolls it, vectorises the body, hoists three invariants out of it, and emits something that bears no visible relationship to the source. When the result is fast this is invisible and welcome. When the result is wrong, the programmer is debugging a program they did not write, using a mental model of a machine that has not existed since the nineteen eighties, and the gap between those two things is where the hardest bugs live.

The letters were sold as a lot at a provincial auction, described in the catalogue as correspondence, nineteenth century, various hands. There were eighty-three of them. Sixty were from a woman to her brother, who had emigrated; the rest were unrelated and had presumably been bundled in to make the lot worth listing. The sixty told an ordinary story of weather, prices, illnesses and a slow estrangement, and they were valuable precisely because nothing in them was remarkable. Almost nobody in that century wrote down what an ordinary week was like.

Tidal power has an unusual property among renewable sources: it is predictable decades in advance. The moon does not have bad years. This ought to make it attractive to grid operators, who spend enormous effort forecasting wind and solar, and yet installed tidal capacity remains negligible. The reasons are unglamorous. Seawater destroys machinery, the best sites are far from demand, and maintenance requires either divers or an expensive lift, none of which improve with scale in the way that manufacturing a solar panel does.

He described the illness as a country he had visited and returned from, and disliked the metaphors other people offered him instead. It was not a battle; nothing had been fought and nothing won. It was not a journey, because a journey implies a destination chosen in advance. It was more like weather, something that had happened to the landscape he already was, and the useful question afterwards was not what it had taught him but what still grew.

The archive's cataloguing standard requires that every photograph be described without interpretation. A picture of a crowd is a crowd, not a protest; a picture of a man at a desk is a man at a desk, not a bureaucrat. The rule exists because interpretations date badly and descriptions do not, and because a researcher searching for something the cataloguer never imagined will find it only if the description stayed close to what is actually visible in the frame.

Glaciers move faster in summer, when meltwater reaches the bed and lifts the ice slightly off the rock. The effect is small in any given week and enormous over a season. It is also self-limiting in a way that surprised the first people to model it: faster flow opens larger channels, larger channels drain the water more efficiently, and the lubricating film thins again. The system oscillates rather than running away, which is a good deal less alarming than the first analyses suggested and considerably harder to summarise in a headline.

Most of what makes a piece of software pleasant to use is invisible when it works. The list scrolls without stuttering. The undo restores exactly what you expected. The error message names the thing you actually did wrong. None of these are features in the sense that anyone would put them on a box, and all of them cost more engineering time than the features that do go on the box, which is a large part of why so much software is unpleasant.

The village had two bakeries for four hundred people, which everyone agreed was one too many and nobody was willing to see close. They sold slightly different bread to slightly different customers, and the overlap was smaller than the arithmetic suggested. When one finally shut, after the older baker retired without a successor, the survivor did not absorb the trade. About a third of it simply stopped: those customers had been buying a walk and a conversation, and the remaining shop was in the wrong direction.
